review.reason: Verified on disk against the pinned-baseline diff: the only code change in src/models/gbm.py is BASE_PARAMS['learning_rate'] 0.05 -> 0.03 with n_estimators held at 400 (gbm.py:29-39, only line 30 changed plus an inline comment), exactly matching the hypothesis of a reduced learning rate with an unchanged bounded tree budget. A repo-wide search for 'learning_rate' found no other occurrence, and BASE_PARAMS is only referenced by the GBMModel default_factory (gbm.py:72) — the variants in src/backtest/run.py:32-37 (including gbm_cal_product_norecency) instantiate GBMModel without overriding params, so the claim in docs/EXPERIMENT.md that the change applies to every GBM variant is accurate. tests/test_candidate.py contains only param assertions (BASE_PARAMS['learning_rate']==0.03, GBMModel().params['learning_rate']==0.03, n_estimators==400 in both); GBMModel() instantiation merely copies the dict via field(default_factory=...), so there is no fit, predict, mock, or training dataframe, as required. I ran the test read-only with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and -p no:cacheprovider: 3 passed, exit 0 — the candidate's test claims are verified, not fabricated. Temporal-leakage review: the diff touches only a static hyperparameter, so it cannot affect data sourcing or time gating; the unchanged fitting logic keeps calibration entirely inside the training window (split = cutoff - holdout_days, gbm.py:123; inner rows gated by y_first_usable <= split at gbm.py:124; calibration holdout rows origin >= split at gbm.py:125), so first_usable precedes holdout origins, there is no validation-target fitting, no test-period labels or recalibration, and no external data. docs/EXPERIMENT.md correctly describes the change and defers all performance claims to the protected host evaluation; no metrics are asserted anywhere. No files were modified during review.
